description: Wire the pipeline into services/api-gateway/src/routes/tracking.ts (depends on FEAT-001). Remove production mock-GPS fallbacks (critical rules), add >30s stale detection, validate + store every GPS observation to gps_observations (valid AND invalid with rejection_reason), ingest valid observations into segment_speed_observations, and add three traffic endpoints: POST /tracking/traffic/predict (15-min cache), GET /tracking/traffic/best-time, GET /tracking/traffic/segments (realtime-from-last-10-min else baseline).
steps: Read services/api-gateway/src/routes/tracking.ts fully. Add `const isProd = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production';` and `const isTest = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'test';` near the top. Gate EVERY mock fallback behind `!isProd`; add `_mock: true` to every mock object. GET /nearby and GET /nearby-drivers: in prod when no real drivers return `{ drivers: [], count: 0, message: 'Hakuna madereva karibu sasa' }`. GET /trip/:tripId and GET /trip/:tripId/driver-location: in prod when no real data return `res.status(404).json({ error: 'Trip/driver location not available' })` (no mock coordinates). GET /traffic: in prod when no real rows return `[]` (200).

Add stale detection to GET /driver/:driverId, GET /trip/:tripId, GET /trip/:tripId/driver-location, GET /nearby, GET /nearby-drivers: compute `const last_seen_seconds = Math.round((Date.now() - updatedAt)/1000);` and include `is_stale: last_seen_seconds > 30` plus `last_seen_seconds` in each driver/location-shaped response (updatedAt is the in-memory loc.updatedAt or the DB last_location_update epoch).

Import `{ validateGpsObservation, GpsObservation }` from `'../services/GpsValidator'` and `{ ingestObservationToSegment, predictTraffic, findBestDepartureTime }` from `'../services/TrafficPredictor'`. Add `async function handleGpsUpdate(userId: string, obs: GpsObservation, pool, trip_id?: string|null)` (exported or local): call `validateGpsObservation(obs, previous)`; run `UPDATE drivers SET current_latitude=$1, current_longitude=$2, last_location_update=NOW(), is_online=true WHERE user_id=$3 RETURNING id`; if a driver id is returned, INSERT into gps_observations(driver_id, trip_id, lat, lng, speed_kmh, heading, accuracy_m, obs_timestamp, is_valid, rejection_reason) for BOTH valid and invalid (invalid sets is_valid=false + rejection_reason); if valid && obs.speed_kmh != null, call `await ingestObservationToSegment({driver_id, trip_id, lat, lng, speed_kmh: obs.speed_kmh, observed_at: new Date(obs.timestamp)}, pool)`. Use handleGpsUpdate in BOTH POST /driver/location and POST /driver/update, building the GpsObservation from the request body: `accuracy_m: body.accuracy` (optional/undefined), `timestamp: body.timestamp ?? Date.now()`. Keep the existing in-memory driverLocations.set and the drivers UPDATE behavior.

Add POST /tracking/traffic/predict: body `{ segment_ids: string[], departure_time: string }`. 400 if segment_ids is missing/empty. Cache 15 min: SELECT segment_id, predicted_speed_kmh, confidence, model_type FROM traffic_predictions_cache WHERE segment_id = ANY($1) AND predicted_for = $2 AND expires_at > NOW(); if every requested segment is cached, return `{ departure_time, predictions: <mapped cached rows incl road_name+status+color+observations_used 0>, cached: true, model_summary }`. Otherwise call `await predictTraffic(segment_ids, departure_time, pool)`; for each result UPSERT into traffic_predictions_cache (segment_id, predicted_for, predicted_speed_kmh, confidence, model_type, expires_at=NOW()+INTERVAL '15 minutes'); return `{ departure_time, predictions, cached: false, model_summary: { ml: count, baseline: count, insufficient_data: count } }`.

Add GET /tracking/traffic/best-time: parse `segment_ids` from query (comma split, filter empty) and `from_time` (ISO; default now). 400 if no segment_ids. Call `await findBestDepartureTime(segment_ids, from_time, pool)` and return its object `{ from_time, best_time, savings_minutes, total_minutes_at_from, total_minutes_at_best }`.

Add GET /tracking/traffic/segments: SELECT id, road_name, lat_start, lng_start, lat_end, lng_end, length_m FROM road_segments ORDER BY id. For each segment, SELECT AVG(observed_speed_kmh)::float AS speed, COUNT(*) AS n FROM segment_speed_observations WHERE segment_id=$1 AND observed_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '10 minutes'. If n>0 -> source 'realtime', current_speed_kmh=speed, status/color from thresholds (<15 jam red, 15-35 slow orange, >35 clear green). Else -> source 'baseline' using current Dar day/hour baseline rules (same rules as TrafficPredictor). Return `{ segments: [{ segment_id, road_name, lat_start, lng_start, lat_end, lng_end, length_m, current_speed_kmh, status, color, source }] }`.
acceptance_criteria: `cd services/api-gateway && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -E 'tracking' | grep -v node_modules` outputs nothing (0 TypeScript errors).

`grep -n 'mock' services/api-gateway/src/routes/tracking.ts` shows every mock array is inside a `!isProd` (or isTest) gated branch and each mock object carries `_mock: true`; no mock data is reachable when NODE_ENV=production.
POST /tracking/traffic/predict, GET /tracking/traffic/best-time, and GET /tracking/traffic/segments are defined in tracking.ts and thus mounted at /v1/tracking/... (no index.ts edit needed).
POST /driver/location and POST /driver/update both validate via GpsValidator and store to gps_observations (valid + invalid), and valid observations feed segment_speed_observations.
verification: cd services/api-gateway && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -E 'tracking' | grep -v node_modules  -> expect empty output
grep -n 'mock' services/api-gateway/src/routes/tracking.ts  -> review: all mock arrays gated behind !isProd and tagged _mock:true
findings: traffic_predictions_cache table needs an ON CONFLICT target; the UPSERT uses ON CONFLICT (segment_id, predicted_for) — migration 016 must include a UNIQUE constraint on (segment_id, predicted_for) for this to work. FEAT-003 should verify that constraint exists or add it. The gps_observations INSERT uses to_timestamp($8 / 1000.0) to convert millisecond epoch; migration 016 obs_timestamp column must be TIMESTAMPTZ. ingestObservationToSegment does a per-observation full road_segments fetch — acceptable for now but FEAT-003 may want to cache this.
